title: Rapid Responder playlet surface: one-click admin shortcuts for incident remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a lightweight surface called 'Rapid Responder' that exposes curated, permissioned admin playlets (small remediate-and-observe tasks) as one-click actions in the Console and as API endpoints for on-call tooling. Goal is to reduce mean time to remediation for common incidents by providing safe, auditable shortcuts that execute validated task sequences (checks, read-only probes, followed by guarded remediations) and attach telemetry to the incident ticket.

Background: On-call workflows currently require running ad-hoc scripts, cross-referencing runbooks, and opening multiple consoles. We've seen repeated patterns for cluster recovery, KV-cache flushes, routing fallbacks, and quota resets. Existing runbook fragments are scattered and often require manual parameter handling, which increases friction and error rate.

Proposal: 1) Define a playlet schema (typed inputs, prechecks, idempotency markers, revert steps) and an execution surface in the Console that shows pre-run validation, required permissions, and expected blast radius; 2) Implement a runtime executor that sequences read-only probes, optional dry-run, and a guarded execution phase with explicit human-approval gating for high-risk actions; 3) Wire telemetry to attach run artifacts (logs, diffs, timestamps) to the originating incident and to the model that suggested the playlet; 4) Provide a minimal REST endpoint for Slack/CLI integrations to invoke the playlets with an approvals trampoline.

Why unique: This is not a generic runbook storage feature. Rapid Responder is a curated, safety-first action surface designed for frequent ops patterns, instrumented for cost/latency/regression analysis, and built with clear PKI/KMS and RBAC constraints for Dedicated/Private environments.
acceptance_criteria: Playlet schema documented and validated with 3 example playlets (cluster-nearby-router-fallback, kv-prefix-evict, dedicated-pool-scale-down-safe)
Console surface prototype shows playlet details, permission check, estimated impact, and execute/dry-run buttons
Executor supports prechecks, dry-run, approval gating, and attaches full telemetry to the incident record
REST endpoint exists for programmatic invocation with audit headers and idempotency token
Security review completed and RBAC/KMS integrations documented
E2E smoke tests exercise at least one playlet in sandbox with rollback
work_notes: 2026-02-21: Kickoff with SRE, Platform and DX. Collected top 10 manual remediation scripts from ops rotation notes.
2026-02-25: Design spike completed for playlet schema. Chose fields: inputs, readOnlyProbes, prechecks, steps[], revertSteps[], approvalLevel, allowedRoles, auditPayloadTemplate.
2026-03-01: Security sync: RBAC flows must use short-lived capability tokens; KMS to sign telemetry bundles. Security requested threat model doc before approval.
2026-03-04: UX session with Support leads. They want predicted SLO impact estimate and an explicit cost token to surface potential token/compute costs for playlet runs.
2026-03-07: Implementation plan reviewed. Blocker: executor sandboxing lib needs upgrades for ephemeral credentials (refer ENG-121212).
2026-03-10: Decided to include a dry-run-only mode by default for first 100 rollouts; telemetry will be opt-out for internal trials. Added label 'pilot:ops-rotation'.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Playlet misuse could cause large-scale impact. Mitigation: multi-tier approvals for high-blast-radius playlets and RBAC enforced at invocation time.
Risk: Leakage of secrets in telemetry. Mitigation: telemetry bundles are encrypted with KMS, scrubbed by default, and stored behind enterprise retention rules.
Risk: Drift between playlet code and underlying infra APIs. Mitigation: include smoke tests in CI and a weekly vetting job that runs read-only probes against canary clusters.
